title: Bhutan Getaway | Black-Necked Crane Festival & Sacred Monasteries
highlights: Celebrate Bhutan's unique traditions on a thoughtfully designed journey featuring the Black-Necked Crane Festival (11 November 2026), monasteries, and Himalayan scenery.
Stay in comfortable, Bhutan Tourism-certified 3-star hotels at an unbeatable price, offering quality stays with warm Bhutanese hospitality throughout the journey.
Experience the Black-Necked Crane Festival in Gangtey, where vibrant masked dances, folk performances, and Bhutanese traditions come alive in a unique cultural celebration.
Explore Bhutan's most iconic destinations, including Thimphu, Gangtey, Punakha, Paro, Tiger's Nest Monastery, and Chele La Pass, with carefully planned sightseeing.
Enjoy seamless travel with well-planned transfers, a dedicated tour leader, and a group tour experience from arrival in Siliguri to departure.
overview:
About the tour:
Discover the timeless beauty of Bhutan on this immersive journey through its peaceful valleys, sacred monasteries, and vibrant cultural traditions. Begin in the charming border town of Phuentsholing before exploring Thimphu's iconic landmarks, ancient monasteries, and living heritage. Venture into the serene Phobjikha Valley to witness the spectacular Black-Necked Crane Festival, where colourful performances and traditional masked dances celebrate Bhutan's rich culture and commitment to conservation. Explore the architectural marvel of Punakha Dzong, visit the revered Chimi Lhakhang, and experience the tranquil landscapes of Punakha. In Paro, conquer the legendary hike to the cliffside Tiger's Nest Monastery, Bhutan's most iconic spiritual landmark, before crossing the breathtaking Chele La Pass with panoramic Himalayan views. Blending authentic festivals, cultural heritage, scenic mountain drives, and unforgettable Himalayan experiences, this journey showcases the very best of the Land of the Thunder Dragon.
inclusions: 2 nights stay in Phuntsholing with breakfast and lunch or dinner
2 nights stay in Thimphu City with breakfast
1 night stay in Gangtey with breakfast
1 night stay in Punakha with breakfast and lunch or dinner
2 nights stay in Paro with breakfast and lunch or dinner
exclusions: Meals not mentioned in the itinerary or inclusions
know_before_you_go: Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.

ID Proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.
Images are for representation purpose only.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

In cases of force majeure events (e.g., natural disasters, political unrest, or other unforeseeable circumstances), [Thrillophilia] reserves the right to reschedule tours & treks or offer alternative itineraries to ensure the safety and well-being of clients and staff.
Please note that prices are dynamic and may change in the peak season and on blackout dates.
Any breakage or damage of any items in the stay property will be charged at actuals.
Please note that the timings and duration of pick-up and drop-off transfers may vary based on certain factors like traffic, weather conditions, natural calamities, etc.
Prices may fluctuate with any change in services/hotels. The difference in the cost shall be borne by the client in case of any amendment in the package due to an increase in the number of guests.

If in case any traveller wants to or decides to leave the trip in the middle, all the expenses from the point onwards will be borne by the traveller. Neither the operator nor Thrillophilia will be held responsible for such decisions or for any refund.
It is recommended that you purchase travel insurance. Please note that the travel insurance is not included in the package price.
Travellers aren't expected to wear the traditional kira, but you should make sure your clothing covers your arms and legs when entering a Dzong.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Phuntsholing | Free Time to Explore
days.desc: Welcome to Siliguri! Upon arrival, board your transfer to Phuentsholing, the charming gateway to Bhutan. Upon reaching, check in to your hotel and relax. Later, you can visit the iconic Bhutan Gate, admired for its traditional Bhutanese architecture, followed by the serene Zangto Pelri Lhakhang, known for its beautiful murals dedicated to Guru Rinpoche. You may also visit the peaceful Gumpha Mandir or head to Alapan View Point to soak in panoramic views of the surrounding hills and landscapes.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Free Time to Explore
days.desc: After check-out, visit the immigration office to complete the permit formalities before beginning your scenic drive to Thimphu, the capital of Bhutan. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel & spend some time relaxing. Later, you can visit the historic Dechen Phodrang Monastery, known for its spiritual significance or you may also explore the National Institute for Zorig Chusum to learn about Bhutan's 13 traditional arts. You can also enjoy a peaceful stroll through the Royal Botanical Garden.

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, set out on a sightseeing tour of Thimphu &visit the National Memorial Chorten, the sacred Changangkha Lhakhang, & other iconic landmarks. Continue to the Motithang Takin Preserve, home to Bhutan's unique national animal, the takin, & learn about its cultural significance. Later, explore the Tashichho Dzong, an fortress-monastery that serves as Bhutan's administrative and religious centre. Also, visit the Royal Textile Museum to discover Bhutan's rich textile traditions and craftsmanship.

days.title: Transfer to Gangtey | Free Time to Explore
days.desc: After checking out from your hotel, board your transfer to the serene Phobjikha Valley and check in to your stay in Gangtey. Later, you can visit the historic Khumbu Lhakhang, a peaceful temple known for its spiritual significance and traditional Bhutanese architecture. In the evening, you can relax with a traditional Bhutanese hot stone bath, a rejuvenating wellness experience where river stones heated over fire are immersed in herbal-infused water to soothe tired muscles after your journey.

days.title: Gangtey Sightseeing Tour | Transfer to Punakha
days.desc: Check-out & explore the scenic Phobjikha Valley. Also, immerse yourself in the vibrant Black-Necked Crane Festival, a unique celebration dedicated to the valley's iconic migratory birds. Witness colourful cultural performances, traditional masked dances, folk music, & conservation-themed events that showcase Bhutan's rich heritage. Later, bid farewell to Gangtey and enjoy a scenic drive through picturesque mountain landscapes to Punakha. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel.

items.title: The Annual Black Necked Crane Festival

days.title: Punakha Sightseeing Tour | Transfer to Paro
days.desc: After checking out from your hotel, explore the cultural treasures of Punakha. Begin with a visit to the magnificent Punakha Dzong, beautifully situated at the confluence of the Pho Chhu and Mo Chhu rivers and admired for its stunning Bhutanese architecture. Continue to Chimi Lhakhang, the revered Fertility Temple dedicated to Lama Drukpa Kunley. Later, admire the tranquil beauty of the Mo Chhu River before embarking on a scenic drive to Paro. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel.

days.title: Hike to Tiger’s Nest Monastery
days.desc: Begin your day with a scenic drive to Satsam Chorten, the gateway to Bhutan's most iconic hike, Tiger's Nest Monastery. Trek through fragrant pine forests lined with colourful prayer flags. Perched on a sheer rock face, this sacred monastery is one of Bhutan's most revered spiritual landmarks. Explore its ancient temples, intricate murals, and meditation caves where Guru Rinpoche is believed to have meditated in the 8th century. Later, descend the trail and get driven back to your hotel.

items.title: Dine-in at the PARK 76 Cafe & Pub
items.label: Suggestion

days.title: Transfer to Phuntsholing | Free Time to Explore
days.desc: After checking out from your hotel, embark on a scenic drive to Phuentsholing via Chele La Pass, the highest motorable pass in Bhutan. Journey through pristine pine and rhododendron forests while soaking in spectacular Himalayan views, with the Mount Jomolhari visible on clear days. Pause to admire the colourful prayer flags fluttering against the mountain backdrop before continuing your descent to the border town. Upon arrival in Phuentsholing, check in to your hotel.

days.title: Departure Day
days.desc: After checking out from your hotel, board your transfer to New Jalpaiguri Railway Station or Bagdogra Airport for your onward journey. Enjoy one last scenic drive through the Himalayan foothills as you bid farewell to the Land of the Thunder Dragon. Carry home unforgettable memories of Bhutan's peaceful monasteries, breathtaking mountain landscapes, colourful cultural festivals, and the warm hospitality that makes this Himalayan kingdom truly special.
